Maria: FYI ran the micro-batcher SLO probe this morning against canary nodes. p50 fine, p95 up ~30% vs baseline, p99 spikes tied to kernel swap events when paged-KV page faults hit. :thinking:
Ajay: do you have a flamegraph or profile snapshot?
Maria: posting a quick perf snippet from the canary machine (trimmed) below:
```
  samples: 2400
  40.1%  runtime_kernel_swap
  25.7%  attention_flash_path
  15.3%  paged_kv_page_fault
  10.0%  batch_formation
  9.0%   io/serialization
```
Sahil: that paged_kv_page_fault number is worrying — looks like eviction latency cascades into batch formation and triggers kernel fallback.
Ryan: is FlashAttention failing over to generic kernel or stalling?
Maria: observed both. When page fault occurs, small-seq requests get demoted to the fallback kernel which has worse throughput -> queue backs up -> micro-batches get greedy and overshoot token budgets.
Liz: can you paste the queue policy config used in the probe?
Maria: config was the new slo-aware policy: max_wait_ms=12, token_budget_target=128, priority=slot_based.
Ajay: token_budget_target=128 seems low for mixed seq lengths, might cause frequent micro-batch flushes when kernel is slow. Suggest adaptive target based on recent kernel RTT.
Sahil: agreed. I sketched an idea: maintain EWMA of kernel per-token latency per model variant, then set token_budget_target = clamp(target_tokens, 32, 1024) where target_tokens = latency_slo_ms / (ewma_per_token_ms * safety_factor).
Ryan: simple formula works on paper. Need to be careful with noisy ewma when page faults are rare but high impact. Maybe add a jail for kernel-switch frequency.
Maria: second problem: when paged-KV faults, reclaim latency shows as blocking syscalls in the flamegraph. We could try prefetching high-KV-hot segments for small-seq traffic on nodes running FlashAttention to reduce faults.
Ajay: prefetching might help but increases memory pressure. Could we instead bias batch formation to coalesce similar KV-hot requests into same micro-batch slot to amortize page hits?
Liz: that sounds promising — batch affinity by KV-heatmap. How do we compute cheaply? maybe a low-res sketch per recent requests.
Sahil: I prototyped a lightweight Bloom sketch keyed by top-n kv pages per session. On canary it reduced paged_kv_page_fault by ~60% for a subset of workloads. Small code snippet:
```
  # pseudocode
  heat_sketch.add(request.kv_page_even_if_partial())
  affinity = heat_sketch.topk(request.session_id)
  assign_to_slot_with_same_affinity(affinity)
```
Ryan: great. Action items: (1) Maria run SLO probe with sketch-affinity and prefetch off-canary, compare p95/p99; (2) Ajay add kernel-RTT EWMA + clamp in batcher and run offline sim; (3) Sahil instrument kernel-switch frequency metric and add alert if > X/min.
Maria: on it — I'll run a 2-hr probe and post results. deploy-bot: starting canary run 1912345678-canary1 now.
deploy-bot: canary launched on cluster gpu-canary-3, id=canary-1912345678.
Liz: also let's log the exact kernel binary versions — just saw one node had a different flash-ops build which may influence the fallback behavior.
Maria: noted. I'll capture binary versions and kernel swap timestamps. Will share a short summary when probe finishes. :thumbsup:
